The [[1948 Winter Olympics]], officially known as the V Olympic Winter Games, were an international multi-sport event held in [[St. Moritz]], Switzerland, from 30 January to 8 February 1948. A total of 669 athletes representing 28 [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOCs) participated. NOCs as first-time entrants at the Winter Games included [[Chile at the 1948 Winter Olympics|Chile]], [[Denmark at the 1948 Winter Olympics|Denmark]], [[Iceland at the 1948 Winter Olympics|Iceland]], [[Lebanon at the 1948 Winter Olympics|Lebanon]], and [[South Korea at the 1948 Winter Olympics|South Korea]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/relive-the-glories-of-past-olympic-winter-games-st-moritz-1948 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816052459/https://www.olympics.com/en/news/relive-the-glories-of-past-olympic-winter-games-st-moritz-1948 |archive-date=16 August 2024 |work=[[International Olympic Committee]] |title=Relive the Glories of past Olympic Winter Games: St.Moritz 1948 |date=1 February 2010 |url-status=live |access-date=26 February 2025 }}</ref> The games featured 22 events in 4 [[Winter Olympic sports|sports]] across 9 disciplines. The games were the first to be celebrated after [[World War II]]; it had been twelve years since the [[1936 Winter Olympics|last Winter Games]] in [[Garmisch-Partenkirchen]], Germany, from 6 to 16 February 1936. The games were the second Winter Games held in St. Moritz.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stillmed.olympics.com/media/Documents/Olympic-Games/Factsheets/The-Olympic-Winter-Games.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130171949/https://stillmed.olympics.com/media/Documents/Olympic-Games/Factsheets/The-Olympic-Winter-Games.pdf |archive-date=30 November 2022 |date=October 14, 2021 |page=1 |title=Factsheet: The Winter Olympic Games |work=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=July 22, 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref>{{sfn|Swiss Olympic Committee|1948|p=13}}

Overall, athletes representing 13 NOCs won at least one medal, and 10 NOCs won at least one gold medal. [[Norway at the 1948 Winter Olympics|Norway]] and [[Sweden at the 1948 Winter Olympics|Sweden]] won the most gold medals with 4 and also won the most overall medals with 10, tied with host nation [[Switzerland at the 1948 Winter Olympics|Switzerland]]. Norway and Sweden also had the same silver and bronze medal totals, meaning that they tied for first place in the medal table.<ref name=sportsref>{{cite Sports-Reference|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/1948/|title=1948 St. Moritz Winter Games|access-date=6 February 2025 |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100402092655/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/1948/|archive-date=2 April 2010 }}</ref> [[Italy at the 1948 Winter Olympics|Italy]]'s team won their first Winter Olympic gold medal after [[Nino Bibbia]] won the [[Skeleton at the 1948 Winter Olympics|men's skeleton event]];<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2013/jun/14/cresta-run-nino-bibbia-david-gower |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220820031430/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2013/jun/14/cresta-run-nino-bibbia-david-gower |archive-date=20 August 2022 |work=[[The Guardian]] |title=How David Gower got it in the neck on a daredevil descent of Cresta Run |date=14 June 2013 |access-date=6 February 2025 |last1=Williams |first1=Richard |authorlink1=Richard Williams (journalist) |url-status=live}}</ref> the medal was also their first Winter Olympic medal of any color.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/countries/ITA |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250120032044/https://www.olympedia.org/countries/ITA |archive-date=20 January 2025 |access-date=6 February 2025 |work=[[Olympedia]] |title=Italy Overview |url-status=live }}</ref> Additionally, [[Belgium at the 1948 Winter Olympics|Belgium]]'s team won their first Olympic gold medal, with [[Micheline Lannoy]] and [[Pierre Baugniet]] winning the [[Figure skating at the 1948 Winter Olympics – Pairs|pair skating event]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.ph/olympics/story/_/id/33326106/belgian-skater-bart-swings-wins-gold-medal-mass-start-beijing-olympics |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240611005155/https://www.espn.ph/olympics/story/_/id/33326106/belgian-skater-bart-swings-wins-gold-medal-mass-start-beijing-olympics |archive-date=11 June 2024 |date=19 February 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |title=Irene Schouten wins speedskating mass start for 3rd gold of Beijing Olympics |url-status=live }}</ref>

Alpine skiers [[Henri Oreiller]] of [[France at the 1948 Winter Olympics|France]] and [[Martin Lundström]] of Sweden tied for the most gold medals won by an individual at the games, with two each. Oreiller also won the most overall medals, winning an additional bronze medal for a total of three medals.<ref name=sportsref /> Norway and Sweden both achieved [[podium sweep]]s at the games, with the former in the [[Ski jumping at the 1948 Winter Olympics|individual ski jumping event]] with [[Petter Hugsted]] winning the gold, [[Birger Ruud]] winning the silver, and [[Thorleif Schjelderup]] winning the bronze, and the latter in the [[Cross-country skiing at the 1948 Winter Olympics – Men's 18 kilometre|men's 18 kilometre cross-country skiing event]] with Lundström winning the gold, [[Nils Östensson]] winning the silver, and [[Gunnar Eriksson]] winning the bronze.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-salt-lake-tribune-summary-for-saturd/164819387/ |date=8 February 1948 |access-date=6 February 2025 |page=41 |work=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |title=Summary for Saturday's Olympic Competition |via=[[Newspapers.com]] }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/st-moritz-1948/results/cross-country-skiing/18km-men |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241204091233/https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/st-moritz-1948/results/cross-country-skiing/18km-men |archive-date=4 December 2024 |title=St. Moritz 1948 Cross Country Skiing 18km Men Results |work=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=6 February 2025 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Medal table==
[[File:Martin Lundström in St Moritz 1948.jpg|thumb|[[Martin Lundström]] tied with Oreiller for the most gold medals won at the games, with two.|alt=Martin Lundström skiing with an audience at the right side.]]
[[File:Nino Bibbia.jpg|thumb|[[Nino Bibbia]], the first Winter Olympic medalist for Italy|alt=A headshot of Nino Bibbia.]]
The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |website=[[The Independent]] | date=11 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |access-date=12 August 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |website=[[The New York Times]] | date=18 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |url-access=subscription |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite web |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |website=[[Diario AS]] | date=10 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=11 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |access-date=11 August 2024 |language=en-us}}</ref> 

In [[Alpine skiing at the 1948 Winter Olympics|alpine skiing]], two bronze medals were awarded in the [[Alpine skiing at the 1948 Winter Olympics – Men's downhill|men's downhill event]] after a third-place tie.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/hartford-courant-winter-olympic-games-su/164819728/ |date=3 February 1948 |page=11 |title=Winter Olympic Games Summary |work=[[Hartford Courant]] |agency=[[United Press]] |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=6 February 2025 }}</ref> In [[Speed skating at the 1948 Winter Olympics|speed skating]], a three-way tie for second place resulted in three silver medals and no bronze medal being awarded in the [[Speed skating at the 1948 Winter Olympics – Men's 500 metres|men's 500 metres event]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-san-bernardino-county-sun-winter-oly/164819837/ |work=[[The San Bernardino Sun]] |agency=[[United Press]] |title=Winter Olympics Settle Down as Strife Subsides; U.S. in Running |last1=Pinkley |first1=Virgil |date=1 February 1948 |page=23 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] }}</ref>
